grammar.title: 叫 for names and calling out
grammar.explanation: 叫 (jiào) means "to be called" when introducing a name, and "to call out to" when the object is a person. 他叫什么? asks what someone or something is called.

grammar.title: 吗 for yes/no questions
grammar.explanation: Adding 吗 (ma) to the end of any statement turns it into a yes/no question, with no change in word order. 你好吗? means "Are you well?" This is a simpler alternative to verb-不-verb questions — don't combine the two in one sentence.

grammar.title: Asking someone's name with 名字
grammar.explanation: 你叫什么名字? ("What's your name?") is the standard way to ask a name, combining 叫 ("to be called") with 名字 ("name"). 名字 can also stand on its own as a noun, as in 他的名字 ("his name").
